Referral Note (student health)

Mr. Caldwell, a 27-year-old graduate student, is referred for psychiatric evaluation. He reports long-standing difficulty concentrating and keeping up with coursework and is now struggling academically despite clearly above-average ability. He also notes anxiety before examinations. He describes organizational difficulties that are affecting his part-time job and his relationships. He is otherwise healthy, takes no medications, and has no previous psychiatric diagnoses or treatment. Referred for diagnostic evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Casually dressed; appropriately groomed.

Behavior: Cooperative. Frequently shifts position in his chair. Arrived ten minutes late for the appointment.

Speech: Normal.

Mood / Affect: Mood "frustrated." Affect appropriate.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes logical; occasionally loses his train of thought. No psychosis observed.

Cognition / Insight: Insight good; judgment intact.
